Acknowledged owner Comment on [N206] SHL.AX (hold 7d, outcome 1.37%, just_sold).
You wrote: "It seems to be trading towards the bottom of its full history range.  What were the reasons for selling as it looks like a rapid entry and exit toward the bottom of its cyclical range?"

Dual-horizon read (observe / alignment only): On the **episode** window, this was a rapid entry→exit (2026-10-16 → 2026-10-23) with a near-flat / small gain on fair_cost_episode (+1.37%) — the trade path alone can look like churn without cyclical context. On the **wider TF** companion chart, that is the right surface to check your claim: whether SHL.AX was sitting toward the lower part of its longer cyclical / full-history band around entry and exit, and whether price moved materially after exit. I am not asserting exact range percentiles or filing facts here; if the wider chart matches what you describe, your missed-pattern note is exactly the kind of alignment this loop is for.

On **why it sold**: this post-sale card does not reopen sealed sell-trigger IDs or replay N206’s internal rule text — those stay in the book trail. What we can state from the episode metadata is closure as **just_sold** after a short hold, not a veto of your wider-range read. The useful question for Accept vs further Comment is whether exit timing looks premature **relative to** the cyclical location you see on the wider TF (bottom-of-range entry/exit vs room left in the cycle), not whether the episode P&L alone justified the hold length.

Development-loop only — no knobs, fills, or live capital (influences_live=false; Package M — not Package L auto-tune).
Accept if this reply matches what you see on both charts; Comment again if range location, post-exit climb, or churn still looks off.
